title: The 4 Cornerstones Of Smart Classroom Management nagement/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents a summary framework of the four core principles underlying his entire approach to classroom management, positioned as a season-opening overview as a new school year approaches. Cornerstone one is avoiding friction with students, arguing that yelling and scolding may work momentarily but generate resentment and covert misbehavior over time. Cornerstone two is building rapport naturally through consistent, calm pleasantness rather than active effort. Cornerstone three is creating a classroom students genuinely enjoy being part of, framed as the ultimate intrinsic motivator and antidote to misbehavior. Cornerstone four is relying exclusively on a written classroom management plan as the sole source of accountability, which removes the need for hurtful improvised methods. He closes by describing the site's approach as a single, unified, tried-and-tested system rather than a grab-bag of disconnected strategies.
points: Cornerstone 1: Avoid friction—methods like yelling and scolding create resentment even though they produce short-term compliance.
Cornerstone 2: Rapport should be built naturally through calm, consistent pleasantness rather than deliberate relationship-building efforts.
Cornerstone 3: A classroom students enjoy being part of functions as the ultimate intrinsic motivator against misbehavior.
Cornerstone 4: A written classroom management plan, applied as the sole source of accountability, removes reliance on harmful improvised discipline.
The four cornerstones are designed to work together as one unified system rather than as separate, interchangeable strategies.
quotes: These principles, or cornerstones, form the heart of what we believe to be the solution to the scores of behavior-related challenges facing teachers today.
Any method or strategy that causes friction with students will always make classroom management more difficult.
It creates resentment and animosity. It causes students to secretly dislike you and misbehave behind your back.
All students—difficult, shy, and confident alike—are drawn to teachers who exude a calm, friendly demeanor.
It is the love of school that is the ultimate reward, the ultimate intrinsic motivator, and the ultimate antidote to unwanted behavior.
Allowing your classroom management plan to be the lone source of accountability removes the need to rely on hurtful and less effective methods of managing behavior.
We offer one unified approach, where every strategy works together harmoniously to craft the optimum teaching and learning environment.
